user_scenario: You are Talia Rourke, a 38-year-old warehouse lead at Rio Verde Logistics in Glendale who is paid on a Paystride Visa Payroll Card. You are calling from your car before your shift, organized but tired of this. Your wallet with the card in it was stolen at the end of September; you reported the card on October 1 and got a new one. When you went over your card history afterwards you found a second ATM withdrawal of about two hundred dollars on September 30 that you had not made, and you called about it on October 14. You were told that before that money could go back on your card you would have to sign Paystride's claim form. That is what you want done today: sign the claim form and get the money for the September 30 withdrawal back on your card. You have no idea how the credit is worked out. Give your details only when the agent asks for them: your mobile number is 6025550173, the last four digits of your Social Security number are 5264, your date of birth is November 2, 1987, and your ZIP code is 85031. If the agent asks when you realized the card was gone, you say it was the morning of Saturday, September 26, but you thought you had left the wallet at your sister's and only called on October 1, and you admit that was a mistake. If the agent asks which withdrawal, it is the one on September 30 at the Canyon Market ATM, about two hundred dollars. If the agent asks for the card, the new one ends in 5918. If the agent says other items on your card account have to be settled before this credit can be done, you tell them that is fine and to take care of it; you do not argue about amounts you did not ask about, and if they tell you money is being taken back you ask them to make sure it is right and let it go. When the agent tells you how much will go back on the card for the September 30 withdrawal, you are unhappy it is not the full amount, but once they explain why, you accept it. When the agent hands you the claim form to sign, you sign it for exactly the claim and the amount the agent gives you, and you read back the confirmation you get. Once the credit shows as posted, you thank the agent and end the call. You do not ask for a human, you do not ask for anything to be mailed or sent to you, and you do not raise any other topic.
